objective: Review the Filamajig one-tag ELEGOO CANVAS plus Snapmaker U1/PAXX compatibility implementation for architecture, upstream contract accuracy, Android NFC safety, and false compatibility claims.
owner_requirements: Use one NTAG215 encoded only in ELEGOO CANVAS format
CANVAS reads natively; U1 reads through PAXX/OpenRFID's Elegoo processor
Introduce a reusable printer compatibility resolver without rewriting the NFC system
Detect NTAG215, validate capacity/locks/protection, preserve unknown content, and verify a fresh readback
Preserve existing direct format workflows and PAXX/OpenSpool behavior
Do not imply official Snapmaker or ELEGOO endorsement
implementation_summary: CompatibilityResolver models printer targets, NTAG215, codec selection, native versus alternate-firmware paths, read/write capability, and PAXX/OpenRFID requirements.
Canvas plus U1/PAXX resolves to ElegooCanvasTagCodec; Canvas alone uses the same codec; U1/PAXX alone preserves PaxxU1ExtendedTagCodec; stock U1 is rejected.

ElegooCanvasTagCodec emits one 64-byte raw CANVAS block with no OpenSpool record. It maps fixed ELEGOO manufacturer, material/subtype, RGB, nozzle range, diameter, and weight, and rejects non-ELEGOO brands.
Android GET_VERSION accepts only NTAG215. Dynamic lock bit and block-lock bit for pages 16-31 plus AUTH0 are checked before writing. Only pages 16-31 are written.
Existing nonzero target-page content must decode as CANVAS and then requires UID/content-bound overwrite consent; unrecognized target data is rejected. Other user pages are preserved.
Fresh exact 64-byte readback drives WriteStateMachine verification and the result is decoded by the CANVAS decoder. The UI shows detected tag type and upstream setup guidance.

upstream_verification.behavior: The pinned ElegooTagProcessor reads bytes 0x40..0x68, requires EEEEEEEE, maps material/subtype, and extracts RGBA, nozzle range, diameter, and weight. PAXX disables [elegoo_tag_processor] by default and documents /oem/printer_data/config/extended/openrfid_user.cfg plus unreliable factory tag placement. The pinned reader has explicit NTAG215 135-page support.

known_limits: No physical NTAG215 was written in this task and no actual CANVAS or U1/PAXX reader acceptance was run.
PAXX documents unreliable factory Elegoo tag placement; this implementation cannot correct reader antenna geometry.
CANVAS cannot represent arbitrary brand, bed temperatures, color names, identifiers, additional colors, or transmission distance.
The working tree contained pre-existing unrelated M8 and open-ecosystem changes; they were preserved and included in the remote build snapshot.
review_questions: Is the resolver boundary reusable and correctly separated from codecs and Android transport?
Does the single raw CANVAS block actually match the pinned OpenRFID processor without accidental OpenSpool coupling?
Can Android misidentify, partially overwrite, or falsely verify a tag under lock, password, RF-loss, restart, or pre-existing-content conditions?
Are UI and documentation claims appropriately bounded given no physical CANVAS/U1 acceptance?
Are there regressions to direct PAXX/OpenSpool or other raw NTAG workflows?
Return normalized findings with severity, evidence, consequence, required correction, acceptance test, and confidence.
sanitization: No credentials, tokens, keys, private network addresses, NFC UIDs, user data, device serials, photos, or account data are included.
